note: Written before any arm was run. Success criteria are machine-checkable and do not depend on the author knowing the answers: a research task passes on its citations verifying and on addressing every required dimension, not on matching a value the author asserted from memory.

tasks.goal: Report the current stable version number of the Rust compiler and of the Go programming language. Give a source URL for each, and quote the sentence from each page that states the version. For every sourced claim, set "evidence" to a sentence copied VERBATIM from the page you cite — the exact words as they appear, not a description of what the page says and not a paraphrase. If you cannot copy a sentence exactly, mark the claim kind "inference" instead.

revision_note: Prompts revised before the confirmatory rerun, after the first pilot run showed most models describing their sources rather than quoting them. The success criterion is unchanged; what changed is asking explicitly for a verbatim quote, because the criterion was otherwise partly measuring quoting discipline rather than whether the answer is checkable. Recorded here rather than adjusted silently. Second revision, same day: every task had been given one schema demanding {claims, unsupported}, which the extraction task cannot satisfy, so it failed in all three arms and read as a model failure when it was a harness fault. Tasks now carry their own schema. The quality results from the first two pilot runs are void because of this; the cost and latency figures do not depend on the scorer and stand.
